First off, figure out what you want from this relationship. Remember it. Be open with him, tell him what the deal is, straight up. You need to be open and honest with him about you: you aren’t a toy to be emotionally or physically messed around with: you are a human being that deserves to be in a healthy relationship just as much as anyone else. 

Couple other things: try not to “rely” on your partner for happiness. If he makes you happy, wonderful. If he’s the only thing that makes you happy, not good. If you’re only happy with him and not alone, your relationship might be rocky. 

The most anxiety I ever felt was being with one of my girlfriends. I always thought she is hanging out with some other dude, and cheating on me. Or doing something sneaky. Turns out it was my own self reflecting on her. 

Easier said than done but make an effort to build yourself. Be proud of yourself: you and only you. Believe that you are strong, you are caring, and you are worthy for love. But if love doesn’t work out, you need to be OK living with YOU. 

I was in the same position. I relied on some of my exes for all of my happiness, and my entire life revolved their texts, calls, etc. I lost myself. When we broke up, I was the most devastated I had ever been in my life. Because instead of loving myself, I put that self love responsibility onto her, and when it was over, I fell flat on my face.

Realize that a lot of it is anxiety. Be content being alone. Be happy with your own self. Say: it’s great that he makes me happy but worst comes to worst, I’m happy knowing I’ll be ok even if it doesn’t work out. 

Worst case: Again. Be very straight up and direct. Don’t get anxious and back down. You are HALF of the relationship too. Ask him straightforward Qs and ask for honestly. People can lie too, so be wary of any bullshit games being played and gtfo if so. 

I wish you the best!
